_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor.
name: Red Eclipse
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Red Eclipse, the free arena shooter with parkour, impulse boosts and many game modes. It also uses the port after the server's port, so add that one too. Other settings are in home/servinit.cfg.
startup: b=; command -v box64 >/dev/null && b=box64; export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$PWD/bin/amd64 BOX64_LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$PWD/bin/amd64 BOX64_LOG=0; exec $b ./bin/amd64/redeclipse_server_linux -h/home/container/home -sp{{SERVER_PORT}}

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Red Eclipse. Downloads a release from GitHub and keeps only what the
# server needs (the server, its config/ scripts and the maps), about 10 MB of
# the 950 MB release. home/ (servinit.cfg, your settings, bans) is never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
build=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
trap 'rm -rf "$build"' EXIT

want=${VERSION:-latest}
[ "$want" = latest ] || want="v${want#v}"
tag=$(gh-release tag redeclipse/base "$want") ||
    fail "Red Eclipse ${VERSION} doesn't exist. Check Version and reinstall."
version=${tag#v}

if [ -x bin/amd64/redeclipse_server_linux ] && [ "$(cat .raptor-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$version" ]; then
    echo "Red Eclipse $version is already installed."
else
    rm -rf "$build" && mkdir -p "$build"
    echo "Downloading Red Eclipse $version (about 950 MB, of which the server keeps 10 MB)"
    gh-release download redeclipse/base "$tag" "redeclipse_${version}_nix.tar.bz2" "$build/re.tar.bz2" ||
        fail "The download from GitHub failed. Reinstall to try again."
    tar -xjf "$build/re.tar.bz2" -C "$build" --wildcards \
        '*/bin/amd64/redeclipse_server_linux' '*/bin/amd64/libsteam_api.so' '*/config/*' '*/data/maps/*' '*/doc/examples/servinit.cfg' ||
        fail "Red Eclipse's download has no Linux server in it."
    rel=$(find "$build" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'redeclipse*' | sed -n 1p)
    mkdir -p bin data
    rm -rf bin/amd64 config data/maps
    mv "$rel/bin/amd64" bin/amd64
    mv "$rel/config" config
    mv "$rel/data/maps" data/maps
    chmod +x bin/amd64/redeclipse_server_linux
    mkdir -p home
    [ -f home/servinit.cfg ] || mv "$rel/doc/examples/servinit.cfg" home/servinit.cfg
    echo "$version" > .raptor-version
fi
# The settings the server's variables set, as lines Raptor rewrites at each
# start (the example servinit.cfg has them commented out).
mkdir -p home
touch home/servinit.cfg
for k in sv_serverdesc sv_serverclients serverpass adminpass; do
    grep -q "^$k " home/servinit.cfg || echo "$k \"\"" >> home/servinit.cfg
done
echo "Installed Red Eclipse $version."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Red Eclipse release, such as 2.0.0, or latest for the newest one. Players need the same release. Reinstall the server after changing it.

variables.name: Server name
variables.description: The name players see in the server browser.

variables.name: Max players
variables.description: How many players can be on the server at once.

variables.name: Password
variables.description: The password players join with. Empty, anyone can join.

variables.name: Admin password
variables.description: The password for /setmaster, which gives a player admin rights. Empty turns it off.
